note: Every README claim, machine-checked. bash scripts/verify.sh runs each command and prints PASS/FAIL; CI runs the same script on every push, so the numbers cannot drift from the code.

claims.claim: A shell redirect is classified as a file edit, never as a read: `echo pwned >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` is file-edit.
claims.command: $PYTHON -c "from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command; assert classify_command('echo pwned >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys').action_class == 'file-edit'"

claims.claim: A greater-than inside quotes is not treated as a redirect.
claims.command: $PYTHON -c "from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command; assert classify_command('grep \"a>b\" notes.md').action_class == 'read'"

claims.claim: Force-pushing a protected branch is denied, in both spellings (--force and the +refspec form).
claims.command: $PYTHON -c "from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command; a = classify_command('git push --force origin main'); b = classify_command('git push origin +main'); assert a.hard_deny and b.hard_deny"

claims.claim: A plain push is not hard-denied; it simply has to be earned.
claims.command: $PYTHON -c "from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command; assert not classify_command('git push origin main').hard_deny"

claims.claim: Three human-approved, verified runs promote a class from L0 to L1 (covered by the gate suite).
The before/after benchmark regenerates its evidence files from scratch.
The CLI produces the one-command self-install prompt for an agent.
